english.title: Adult permit child or young person to enter adult gaming centre premises - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) permitted a

(A)_[child]_
(B)_[young person]_

aged **(..SPECIFY AGE..) to enter premises where an adult gaming centre premises licence had effect in respect of the premises, and the premises were being used in reliance on that licence when the

(C)_[child]_
(D)_[young person]_

was permitted to enter
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 47(5) and 62(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording applies to adults, aged 18 or over, only; for young persons see the offence wording GA05091/H8270.
(ii) Section 45 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "child" means an individual who is less than 16 years old, and "young person" means an individual aged 16 or 17.
(iii) Section 63 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides the defence of reasonable belief about a person's age.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
